newsitem.title: USA: Layne Christensen in pact to build barrier.
newsitem.headline: Layne Christensen in pact to build barrier.

text.p: Layne Christensen Co, a drilling services company, said Monday it has entered a contract worth about $27 million to construct an artificial ground freezing barrier around an Echo Bay Mines Ltd gold mine.
The project will provide what Layne Christensen said is the world's largest artificial ground freezing barrier, around the Aquarius Gold Mine in Timmons, Ontario.
The wall, designed to remain frozen for seven years, involves drilling about 1,900 wells and installing freezing pipes circulating 5,000 tons of refrigerant, Layne Christensen said.
The wall is a substitute for dewatering the site over the life of the mine.

"This is clearly the most environmentally compatible solution as the barrier will leave the groundwater table and surrounding lakes unaffected," Greg Aluce, vice president of Layne Christensen's environmental, specialty services and geotechnical construction groups said in a news release.
Layne Christensen shares were down 1/4 at 19-3/4 Monday.
